title: The Ceiling Inverts the Borough
gallery_text: The programme lends at most $220,000, so the lots with the most room fail first - a full-size unit costs more than the loan will cover. The grant is set to zero here, which is the version of the programme that exists if nobody funds it.
description:
Two things are changed from the published terms: the grant is zero, and the map is flat so the pattern can be read.

At the real grant of $175,000, 62% of eligible lots clear the cushion. At zero, 12% do. The lots that survive are the small ones in the northwest of the borough, because a smaller yard means a smaller unit, a smaller cost, and a loan that fits under the $220,000 ceiling. The eastern lots have the most room and fail first.

Nothing in the term sheet says the programme is for dense neighbourhoods. It falls out of the arithmetic, and it is the ceiling that does it rather than the rent.
